title: GPU cluster autoscaler compatibility shim and Terraform module for Private VPC
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our Private (VPC) deployment runs multiple GPU-backed nodepools across regions; customers have requested predictable autoscaling behavior with both ASG-backed pools and Karpenter-based pricing-optimized pools. Existing Terraform modules are fragmented: ASG-centric modules assume public subnets and do not include the Karpenter CRD bootstrap or health-check hooks required for our private control plane. Upgrades of GPU AMIs and drivers are fragile when mixed autoscalers are present.

Goal: Create a single opinionated Terraform module that provisions GPU node groups in Private VPCs and exposes an autoscaler compatibility shim so teams can declaratively bind the same node group resources to either ASG or Karpenter. The module should: 1) support private subnet placement and ENI/sg rules, 2) include lifecycle hooks and health-check endpoints for graceful drain and driver upgrades, 3) emit consistent tags/annotations used by routing and billing, 4) provide a documented fallback policy for autoscaler unavailability, and 5) include a small controller manifest and bootstrap scripts for Karpenter integration.

Deliverables:
- terraform module sources (module interface + examples) for asg and karpenter usage
- small compatibility shim (helm/kustomize manifests + init script) to ensure Karpenter node templates are consistent with ASG node labels
- CI plan with integration tests in a Private staging account (upgrade/scale/drain scenarios)
- runbook for rolling driver/AMI upgrades and rollback criteria

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement cross-region federation for autoscalers or change billing pipelines. It focuses on Terraform module API and runtime behavior in Private VPCs.

2026-02-18 - Marcus Chen: Design review notes - prefer explicit node-template outputs instead of encoding labels into tags. Raised concern about Karpenter bootstrap needing access to S3 (driver artifacts) in private subnets; suggested pre-populating ECR/S3 endpoints via VPC endpoints.

2026-02-23 - Design (Sofia Rodriguez): Approved high-level API. Requested UX change: expose a 'maintenance_window' attribute to schedule non-disruptive upgrades. Also asked that examples include a dedicated 'eks + karpenter' example path.

2026-02-28 - Marcus Chen: Implemented terraform module skeleton. Key decisions: use a small 'compat-shim' daemonset that translates ASG tags to node labels for Karpenter discovery; the shim will run with hostPID= false and minimal privileges. Added lifecycle hooks via SQS+Lambda backed draining for ASG path to call the same health-check endpoint used by the shim.

2026-03-03 - QA (Diego Martinez): Ran integration scenario: scale up to 100 pods scheduled across mixed GPU pools. Observed cold-start latency spikes when Karpenter pod provisioning first-time pulls large driver blobs. Action: add pre-warm container image pull using init job during node bootstrap. Filed follow-up ENG-776744.

2026-03-06 - Security (Priya Nair): Reviewed bootstrap scripts and IAM roles. Requested KMS-encrypted S3 usage for driver artifacts and a tighter IAM role for the compatibility shim. Marked security_review_required = true and asked for checklist entries in the runbook.
